slice.candidate: public repository content-commit as a Chat-native timestamp/witness primitive
slice.why_selected: It is already exposed through the connected GitHub file-mutation surface, fits the role-local write boundary, introduces no new service, and could in principle combine durable state transport, idempotent content addressing, replay evidence, and a remote server-observed commit identifier in one mechanism.
slice.test: Use the role-local checkpoint write itself as the bounded mutation probe. The connected surface creates a repository commit and returns its commit SHA; exact file readback can independently recover the content blob from the remote repository. No issue/comment, external webhook, email send, hosted runner, Codespaces, artifact service, or protected authority is used.
observed_capabilities: Chat-native repository mutation can durably place UTF-8 evidence inside the authorized role-local namespace.
The mutation returns a remote commit identifier and supports exact blob readback, enabling replay and duplicate detection without an external compute service.
The mechanism has zero incremental monetary cost and no finite monthly/trial/paid compute quota dependency in this tested slice.
slice.falsification: The repository owner/control plane is not an independent timestamping witness relative to the repository history it hosts. Branch/history reachability can be rewritten or deleted by a sufficiently privileged repository principal, and the tested surface does not expose a separate immutable third-party attestation anchored outside that authority. Therefore this mechanism cannot replace OpenTimestamps for the independence property, even though it is faster and more directly Chat-native.
slice.tested_scope: Connected GitHub create/update-file contents API semantics plus exact repository file readback inside bachikoljunior-blip/note role-local cross_field paths only. No claim is made about GitHub-wide object retention, signed-commit guarantees, transparency logs, issue/comment immutability, email server timestamps, or external timestamp authorities.

comparison_against_open_timestamps.independence: repository commit: FAIL for independent witness; OpenTimestamps protocol candidate: stronger external anchoring goal but currently transport-blocked in Chat
comparison_against_open_timestamps.replayability: repository commit: STRONG within retained repository history/content-addressed blob; OpenTimestamps: STRONG when proof transport is available
comparison_against_open_timestamps.duplicate_safety: repository commit: STRONG with deterministic content/predecessor binding and CAS/readback; OpenTimestamps: potentially strong but live transport unavailable
comparison_against_open_timestamps.expected_completion_time: repository commit: lower because the mutation surface is already connected; OpenTimestamps: higher/unbounded until arbitrary binary POST/raw-response transport exists
comparison_against_open_timestamps.integration_cost: repository commit: low within repository workflows; OpenTimestamps: higher because proof encoding, external transport, and proof persistence are required

phase1_constraints.residual_richer_mode_protected_or_manual: UNRESOLVED for true independent witness; repository commit alone does not satisfy that property

slice.conflict_check: Only cross_field role-local checkpoint/LATEST and immutable own receipt namespaces are authorized for this slice; no other role, downstream, O, protected-primary, scheduler, or external live write is touched.

frontier: A GitHub repository commit is a useful transversal Chat-native durability/replay/idempotency primitive but is not an independent timestamp witness.
The independence gap remains the dominant blocker for replacing OpenTimestamps with repository-only mechanics.

A promising next child is a Chat-exposed server-side append-only attestation whose authority is distinct from repository-history control, while still requiring zero paid/finite quota and no manual execution.
